answer: Operator-linked collateral clawback ties each identity to a raven-signed custody record, so Sybil clusters share one withdrawable reserve. When duplicate behavior is detected, the protocol freezes that reserve and pays bounties from it, meaning the operator loses real capital per fake identity rather than a disposable wallet. A zephyr-latency challenge window lets honest operators contest flags before slash execution. Each attempted duplicate costs the attacker the posted basalt-denominated deposit plus forfeited future rewards, scaling linearly with cluster size.
